newsitem.title: UK: Oil tanker rates flat, not stirred by N.Sea gales.
newsitem.headline: Oil tanker rates flat, not stirred by N.Sea gales.

text.p: Crude oil tanker chartering activity was quiet on Wednesday and gales in the North Sea, which affected some loading operations, failed to affect rates, brokers said.

Middle Eastern markets were quieter after at least three ultra large crude carriers (ULCCs) were fixed on Tuesday for U.S. destinations. "It has been quieter today... those fixings yesterday were a flash in the pan," one dealer said.
Two 250,000 tonne very large crude carriers were fixed for Taiwan at a robust W64 and W65, some five or six points higher than previous fixtures.
Brokers said these two ships, the Sea Duchess and the Bourgogne, were very new and as such commanded good premius.

This week's steady stream of fixtures from West African markets appeared to continue with four new million-barrel fixtures seen for different destinations. But rates have failed to rise, as the tonnage still on offer remains high.

Mediterranean markets were quiet and demand, at least for 80,000 tonne Aframaxes in the first half of the month, is now limited. But supply is short too and any new demand for ships emerging later in the month may find rates rising. "I think this market could go up," one broker said.
Gale force winds of up to 40 knots in the North Sea, which caused a short loading delay at Hound Point, failed to push up dirty tanker rates because of the surplus tonnage available.
"The market is very bad in the North Sea," said another broker who added that the older (80,000 tonne) Aframaxes were fetching W92.5, with new vessels around five points higher.

A fuel oil tanker delayed for two days at Milford Haven had little impact on rates as supplies of Russian fuel oil dry up with the onset of winter, creating a surfeit of vessels. Rates for 25,000 tonne fuel oil tankers were down at W180.
